ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, $AB \perp CD$, and $AB = CD$, $CE \perp AD$ at $E$, $BF \perp AD$ at $F$. Given $CE = 6$, $BF = 3$, $EF = 2$, what is the length of $AD$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Since $AB\perp CD$, $CE\perp AD$, and $BF\perp AD$,\\
it follows that $\angle A+\angle D=90^\circ$, $\angle C+\angle D=90^\circ$, and $\angle CED=\angle AFB=90^\circ$,\\
thus, $\angle A=\angle C$,\\
in $\triangle ABF$ and $\triangle CDE$,\\
$\begin{cases}
\angle A=\angle C \\
\angle AFB=\angle CED \\
AB=CD
\end{cases}$,\\
therefore, $\triangle ABF\cong \triangle CDE$ (AAS),\\
hence, $AF=CE=6$, $BF=DE=3$,\\
therefore, $AD=AF-EF+DE=6-2+3=\boxed{7}$.

First describe the image: In the figure, the bottom side AD is a horizontal line, and the order of the points is A, E, F, D. CE goes vertically upward from point E, and BF goes vertically upward from point F, so CE ⟂ AD and BF ⟂ AD. AB is an oblique line from A to B toward the upper right, and CD is an oblique line from C to D toward the lower right. The figure also marks AB ⟂ CD.

Then reason: Because CE and BF are both perpendicular to AD, △ABF and △CDE are right triangles with right angles at F and E respectively. Also because AB ⟂ CD and CE ⟂ AD, the acute angle formed by AB and AD is equal to the acute angle formed by CD and CE, that is, ∠BAF = ∠DCE. It is known that AB = CD, so △ABF ≅ △CDE (AAS). Corresponding sides are equal, so AF = CE = 6, and DE = BF = 3. From the order A-E-F-D in the figure, AD = AF + FD, while FD = DE - EF = 3 - 2 = 1. Therefore AD = 6 + 1 = 7.
